_README: Decisions taken on the PR 570 findings ledger. HAND-EDITED; the ledger itself is generated.
Key = row id from the ledger (A05, D55, E01, ...). Absent = still open.
accepted -> commits us to the work; give `task`
declined -> we will not do it; `reason` is MANDATORY
deferred -> not now; `until` names the TRIGGER and is MANDATORY, not a date
The generator hard-fails on a key that matches no row, on an unknown status, and on a
declined/deferred missing its reason/trigger. Run scripts/pr570-ledger.py after editing.

A05.note: sector-unload use-after-free. The unload loop now takes m_lightMapPrepMutex, which the gather already holds -- no new lock, 93-276us of main-thread stall. Root cause of the reachability is #127's grid-size bucket widening the calc region on the max side only while neededSectors stayed on the unbucketed window; the false containment comment is replaced by the arithmetic plus counter lighting.gather.calc_outside_loaded. Correct by construction and 346 tests green, but the race was never observed firing -- no TSan preset, jemalloc conflicts with TSan. That verification is deferred on #210, NOT claimed.

A07.note: unguarded GL 4.0 sample-shading. Our fix is a guard, NOT their deletion -- #151 measured the quality at 22.3% of pixels and kept it.

E05.note: same finding as A05, reached from the other direction. Closed by the same commit.

D55.note: vcpkg overlay ports registered nowhere -- the root cause of the build blocker, not the jemalloc patch.

E07.note: register the overlay declaratively; folded into #196's four-step sequence.

C16.note: closed-form assertions. The judge's 'production IS the oracle' was REVERSED by the challenge; what survives is that a differential oracle pins drift, not truth.

C17.note: the CI half is closed -- the lighting tests now run in core_tests on every push, asserted at 257->277 and guarded at configure time. The production-additions-for-testability half remains under #215.

D31.note: the two calculatePointLighting specializations are 2 lines apart, one of them a real beam-epsilon divergence. 8 transcriptions -> 7, not -> 2.

C07.reason: Not a real convergence -- verified converged=false. They rewrote CellularLightArray::calculate(); our default skips it entirely when GPU lighting is latched (StarWorldClient.cpp:2401). Their patch optimises a stage we do not execute.

C08.note: 455 of 1207 lines (38%) of the lighting-array TU is oracle scaffolding. Relocate, do not delete.

C09.reason: Same non-convergence as C07. Their 4.1x-slower GPU result is on Atom-class ADL-N with per-light dispatches, atomicMax, fixed K=48 and full resolution; ours is one raster solve at tile resolution with adaptive K, measured 744us. The finding it DOES carry is recorded on #161.

D13.until: #161 is picked up -- the CPU spread+point cost is the thing their bandwidth analysis is about, and #161 now carries the re-ranked candidate list and the K-sweep measurement that should precede any of it.

D59.note: Trigger met by E10 and executed in #220. tinyformat.h deleted with both companion edits.

D60.note: Trigger met by E10 and executed in #220. lib/linux/libcrypto.a deleted; no build-system edit needed and the lib/ search path deliberately left alone (see D34).

C05.note: The fork was the SINK, not the region -- C05's own framing understated it. gatherColumns(region, sink) holds the per-tile arithmetic once; gatherStableColumns 45 lines -> 12. Byte-identical, proven by the render-gate A/B (both legs hash 471488eed310861f) and by a line-for-line textual diff of the arithmetic.

C11.note: 8 transcriptions -> 7. The challenge UNDERSTATED the gap: 8 vs 2, not 4 vs 1. The other six are not duplication.

C14.reason: The challenge phase WITHDREW this concession: simplicity theirs -> TIE. Its premise ('== "main" cannot be re-broken from asset data') is false, and theirs is provably a no-op for every asset they ship while ours fixes a path live in stock play.

B21.note: rm-lighttraits-spread-multiply. SPLIT THE SLUG. `multiply` is verified dead in our tree -- 2 decls + 2 inline defs in StarCellularLightArray.hpp, ZERO call sites repo-wide (every other `multiply` hit is Color::multiply, ItemDescriptor::multiply, PremultiplyInto, or a Lua/directive string). Deleted at 0a8fff9d. REJECT the `spread` half of their removal: `spread` is LIVE here with 12 call sites in calculateLightSpread plus the Jacobi oracle mirror; they could only delete it because the same patch rewrote the spread sweep to raw channel floats, and rewriting ours is a separate decision that must clear the byte-identity oracle.

B08.note: point-light-cap-and-cull. Their cap+cull is real and survives to their head; we carry NEITHER. DUPLICATE of open row D29 (cap) and B25 (cull) -- one change enumerated three times. Folded into D29, not filed separately. Two flaws named so we do not imitate them: their cull tests the RAW world position with no geometry wrap (the same failure class #217 just fixed in our border estimator), and their cap ranks by raw brightness, so a bright off-screen light outranks a dim one at the player's feet, while the partition reorders the light list and changes the lightmap bitwise even below the cap. Our exposure is per-light draw calls, not wrong pixels: both executors already skip off-grid lights. Size it from lighting.lights.point and lighting.gpu.point.lights before building anything.

B13.reason: COVERED by D59, and confirmed rather than restated: tinyformat.h is dead here (49 KB, zero tfm:: uses). NEW: the deletion needs two companion edits in the SAME commit or configure hard-fails -- source/extern/CMakeLists.txt (star_extern_HEADERS feeds ADD_LIBRARY) and doc/OPENSOURCE.md (licence attribution). Their own PR proved this: patch 0001 deletes the header without the CMake entry and does not configure; patch 0002 repairs it.

B14.reason: COVERED by D59. Same hunk as B13 counted twice -- the CMakeLists entry IS the companion edit B13 requires, not an independent claim.

B15.reason: COVERED by D60, confirmed: lib/linux/libcrypto.a is 4 MB and unreferenced here.

B16.reason: NOT_REAL as applied to us, and actively harmful if taken literally. The lib/linux search path is NOT an implicit link path to be removed -- it is load-bearing for cmake/FindSteamApi.cmake and cmake/FindDiscordApi.cmake. D60's deletion needs no build-system edit at all.

B17.reason: COVERED by D61/E09/#196. mimalloc is NOT dead in our tree: source/vcpkg.json is consumed by source/CMakeLists.txt and source/core/StarMemory.cpp under STAR_USE_MIMALLOC. Deleting it reproduces here the exact configure break their PR scored against itself. The real item is manifest SHAPE -- make the allocator a vcpkg manifest feature (E09), not a deletion.

B18.reason: NOT_REAL. Follows B17: there is no residual build path to remove because the dependency is live.

B22.reason: COVERED by A07/#211. We refuse the deletion outright -- #151 measured per-sample shading at 22.3% of pixels and kept it deliberately. Our fix is a GL 4.0 capability guard.

B04.reason: COVERED by open row D45 (runtime VSync toggle, we-lack-entirely). Not a defect; a feature we do not have. Decide it at D45, not here.

B02.reason: COVERED by #196. Same wall: jemalloc versus libstdc++ 16 blocks a pristine Linux bootstrap on this workstation. Their approach addresses their toolchain, not ours.

B11.reason: COVERED by D65 (closed different-tradeoff). True that build_windows has no persisted vcpkg binary cache, but this was already enumerated and closed. NOTE: B11 and B27 are ONE hunk (+5/-7, patch 0003) counted twice by the enumerator.

B12.reason: COVERED by D59 + D60 + D61/E09 + D64/E10 -- no new finding survives. Their own provenance doc is false on the day it lands (README claims vcpkg.json is pinned by builtin-baseline; their vcpkg.json has no builtin-baseline, removed by their own hand). That contradiction is a concrete argument FOR E10's generated-and-gated form, and is the one element folded forward.

B25.reason: REAL_BUT_NOT_OURS on verification (initially filed as ours, then refuted). Their 49-tile cull radius exceeds the 32-tile windowMonitoringBorder band that bounds our client entity map, so it would drop nothing here -- the server destroys client slaves outside window.padded(32). The 'lantern 80 tiles off-screen' scenario is unreachable in our tree.

B24.reason: REAL_BUT_NOT_OURS. Same single change as B08/D29, third enumeration. Decide the cap at D29.

B01.reason: REAL_BUT_NOT_OURS. We already carry the equivalent as m_lightingTileEpoch with all four of its sites live; their tile-version counter is the same idea reached independently.

B19.reason: REAL_BUT_NOT_OURS. Their file removal follows their own rewrite; our StarCellularLightArray.cpp is live production plus the differential oracle (see #215 for the oracle's relocation, which is the real item here).

B23.reason: REAL_BUT_NOT_OURS. Our AA confinement was settled at C13/C14/C15 and RT-1/#151 -- our undeclared-is-single-sample default already fails safe, which their rule does not.

B10.reason: REAL_BUT_NOT_OURS. Checked our clip-rect handling directly; the unset-sentinel shape they fix is not present here.

B34.reason: REAL_BUT_NOT_OURS as a defect, but it is the evidence for B13's companion edit: their attribution was left behind because their grep was scoped to source/. Ours must include doc/OPENSOURCE.md. Recorded on B13's note rather than actioned separately.

B35.reason: REAL_BUT_NOT_OURS. A measurement claim about their own diff, not a code change: clang-format churn inflates their reported deletion counts. Affects how we read their headline numbers, nothing in our tree.

B20.reason: NOT_REAL as filed, and the perf pivot rests on two errors about our tree. It is an `rm-` claim but concedes it is a layout rewrite, and our AoS Cell store is the live backing store of the whole lighting system -- the opposite of dead. The cost model also counts snapshotSpreadInput as a production reader; it is TEST-ONLY (four callers, all in source/test), so the 'walked twice' figure overstates the real cost 2x. There is exactly one production reader, exportSpreadInputs, under `if (lightingGpu)`. If AoS->SoA is ever revisited it is a measured lever, not a cleanup.

B31.reason: NOT_REAL for us, and COVERED by C05/#214. lightingTileGather() is NOT dead code here: it is the live OFF branch of the lightingGatherCache kill-switch, declared default-true in StarRootLoader, reported in the /lighting status line, and toggled in-process by `/lighting gathercache off`. It is the A/B baseline that de-risks A1/A2. The duplication is real and is #214's job; deleting the lever is not.

B27.reason: NOT_REAL. Their patch 0003 is a REPLACEMENT (+5/-7), not a removal -- the commented block is swapped for a live actions/cache step. Same hunk as B11. And our commented lines are not dead code but a DATED DECISION RECORD: git blame attributes them to a commit whose own subject says the cache was temporarily disabled.

B29.reason: NOT_REAL. The Dial flood fill never appears in the PR: zero hits for bucketHeads/dial in full.diff outside their Russian TODO prose, and zero in their head tree. Settled by absence, which is what the slug itself claims ('invisible'); their patch-0005 message describes why they reverted it. Nothing to learn beyond what C09 already recorded about Xiaolin-Wu.

B32.reason: NOT_REAL. Intra-PR: an API they added earlier in this same PR and then deleted. Worth nothing to us.

B30.reason: NOT_REAL. Within-PR revert with net zero effect -- patch 0002 flips asyncLighting false->true, patch 0005 flips it back true->false; the line is CONTEXT in full.diff. Separately, the sector-unload race this sits beside is CLOSED in our tree at #210/66ec860b.

B06.reason: NOT_REAL. Their lightmap upload version gate repairs a defect introduced earlier in the same PR.

B26.reason: NOT_REAL. Same intra-PR shape; and our #127 stable grid plus #125 VBO orphaning already cut upload churn on this path.

B07.reason: NOT_REAL. The fullbright regression they fix is one they introduced with the version gate itself.

B09.reason: NOT_REAL for us. Lightmap buffer reuse is already served by our existing allocation path; their gain is against their own pre-PR state.

B05.reason: NOT_REAL. Their HDR layout claim is unsupported by their own tree.

B03.reason: NOT_REAL for us. A Windows-only test dump path issue in their harness; our test binaries run from dist/ and do not take that path.

B28.reason: NOT_REAL. Removal of their own Russian-language dev notes, added by patch 0002 and deleted by patch 0008. Pure intra-PR housekeeping -- though the notes were the single most useful artefact in the snapshot for establishing their intent.

A06.reason: Closure STANDS -- their flip/revert is net-zero and we carry no defect -- but the recorded reason is WRONG and the correction matters. It said we 'sit at the upstream default'. We do not: UniverseClient::connect calls setAsyncLighting(true) UNCONDITIONALLY at the sole WorldClient construction site, on both the singleplayer and multiplayer paths, so ASYNC LIGHTING IS ON IN EVERY SESSION and the ctor default (m_asyncLighting = false) is dead code. /asyncLighting is the opt-OUT, not the opt-in. A reversal was filed on this and REFUTED: its claimed payoff, that '#210 was triaged as sitting behind a dormant opt-in path', is false -- A05 was rated real|we-still-have-it|FIX and fixed the same day at 66ec860b. So: no defect, no task, but never again reason about lighting-thread concurrency from that ctor default.

A09.reason: Closure stands, reason NARROWED (reversal upheld by a second pass). We carry no accumulation surface: the A1/A2 gather grid holds INPUT, is written by assignment, and applyStableToCells rewrites 100% of the calc region into a freshly-cleared array every recompute -- so a seam cannot compound. TWO CORRECTIONS to the recorded reason: (1) it calls the A2 cache 'the gathered tile material / env-light grid'; env-light is deliberately EXCLUDED (stableLight omits environmentLight, the skyExposed bit re-applies it per frame) -- that exclusion is the whole point of A1. (2) 'no scroll' should read 'no scroll in the light ARRAY'; we do scroll one level up in shiftAndGatherMargin. The row never examined the INPUT-side staleness of that scroll -- the cache key is (epoch, dims, anchor) and does not track sector load/unload, and unloadSector bumps no epoch. That residual is already instrumented by lighting.gather.calc_outside_loaded (#210) and is E01/E04 territory, not a new defect.

A10.reason: Closure stands, reason NARROWED and its stated premise REFUTED (reversal upheld). What actually closes it: CellularLightArray::begin unconditionally zero-fills the ENTIRE array every recompute and there is no scroll or incremental path, so no cell state survives a window move. What is FALSE: the claim that our point phase 'runs over the whole padded array rather than being window-scoped'. It does not -- our point pass is clipped to the query rect and skips the 32-48 cell border on every side, structurally the SAME geometry as theirs. Also strike 'fully re-solved every lighting update': the point pass is query-scoped, and under the shipping GPU config the CPU calculate() is skipped outright by skipCpuCalc. Kill the window-scope sentence before it propagates -- it would make a future reviewer conclude we differ structurally when we do not.

A12.reason: Closure stands, reason NARROWED (reversal upheld). No defect: CellularLightArray::begin clears m_spreadLights and m_pointLights with no early return, and lightingCalc's only two early returns both sit ABOVE that begin() and above the add loops, so no list is ever appended across frames. But a load-bearing clause of the recorded reason was FALSE WHEN WRITTEN, not merely stale: 'no per-frame point-light bookkeeping to leak' and 'our public API stops at begin/addSpreadLight/addPointLight/setLight/setObstacle/calculate'. We DO have the structural analogue -- exportPointLights feeding m_pendingLightingPointLights, swapped at publish -- shipped since 2026-07-19, before the analysis. THE METHOD FAILURE IS THE FINDING: the row was dismissed by grepping for THEIR identifiers and finding zero hits. A name-grep cannot see an analogue we named differently. Dismissal-by-name-grep is unsound; dismiss on MECHANISM.

D30.note: Both halves settled. The sector-unload race IS the defect and it is fixed at 66ec860b (#210). The asyncLighting half was closed by the A06 sweep: async lighting is unconditionally ON in every session (UniverseClient::connect calls setAsyncLighting(true) at the sole WorldClient construction site, on both paths), the ctor default is dead code, and /asyncLighting is the opt-OUT. No defect in the default; the row stayed open only because nobody folded the two answers together.

D34.note: ACCEPTED, not declined -- the first pass mislabelled this. tinyformat.h (49 KB, zero tfm:: uses, zero includes) and lib/linux/libcrypto.a (4.0 MB, zero references in any CMakeLists/cmake) are both verified dead and are DELETED in #220. D59/D60 had deferred this on the trigger 'someone is already touching source/extern for another reason' -- accepting E10 (a provenance table FOR source/extern) fires that trigger, so the deletions ride with it. Two companion edits were mandatory and are included: source/extern/CMakeLists.txt (tinyformat.h was in star_extern_HEADERS, which ADD_LIBRARY consumes -- a header listed but absent is a configure hard-error, which their own PR proved by shipping patch 0001 without it) and doc/OPENSOURCE.md (licence attribution). The lib/ search path is UNTOUCHED: B16 filed removing it and that is NOT_REAL -- it is load-bearing for cmake/FindSteamApi.cmake and cmake/FindDiscordApi.cmake.

D64.reason: DUPLICATE of E10, which is the same item stated as a concrete recommendation. Decided there, accepted, not lost.

D22.reason: Same ground as C07/C09. Their incremental point-light diff (signed +/-1 flood) optimises the CPU CellularLightArray propagation -- a stage our default configuration does not execute, because skipCpuCalc takes the GPU latch. Not a convergence, so there is no gap to close.

D45.reason: A runtime VSync toggle is a player-facing settings feature, not a defect and not a performance item. Unrelated to the render/perf campaign, and it adds a settings surface we would then own. Director's call, taken 2026-08-04. Reopen if VSync ever needs to be changed without a restart for a measurement reason.

D29.until: lighting.lights.point and lighting.gpu.point.lights have been read from a real play session. We carry no cap and no cull; the exposure is per-light draw calls and uniform sets, NOT wrong pixels, because both executors already skip off-grid lights. A cap built without those numbers is a guess. If it is ever built, take only the idea: rank by contribution to the visible region via CellularLightingCalculator::pointBorderFor, never their raw-brightness sort, and wrap through m_geometry.nearestTo before any distance test -- their cull tests an unwrapped position, which is the exact failure class #217 fixed.

D11.until: #214 lands. A differential oracle for the scroll path cannot be written against the current fork between lightingTileGather and gatherStableColumns; #214 region-parameterises the gather and is what makes one oracle cover both.

E01.note: Trigger fired: #214 landed at 9429b14d, so there is now one gather to extract the scroll math from rather than two forked ones.

E04.note: Trigger fired with #214. The oracle must drive the scroll path, not just the full gather -- which is why E02's counters land first.

E02.note: Meter the gather-cache outcome (hit/scroll/full + reason). REPOINTED from #214 to #221: it was accepted against #214 and not implemented there, so closing #214 orphaned it. It is the instrument E01/E04 are judged by and goes first.

E03.note: Zero only the vacated L-region. REPOINTED from #214 to #221 for the same reason -- accepted against #214, not implemented there.

E06.note: ACCEPTED BUT RE-SCOPED, and the re-scope is the finding. As written it cross-checks 'multisampled: true' against effects' frameBufferTextures -- a set that is EMPTY in our tree, so the guard as specified would catch nothing. The real in-tree path is the C++ source argument to setEffectTextureFromTarget / composite. There is exactly one live candidate, StarBackdropPass composing "main" into parallaxRef, and it is closed only by a two-file coupling nothing asserts: 'main is multisample iff antiAliasing' lives in the renderer + opengl.config, 'the parallax cache path runs iff !antiAliasing' lives in BackdropPass. If the parallax AA gate is ever relaxed -- #151 considered it, #138/P-3 may revisit it -- that composite binds a multisample texture to a sampler2D and reproduces #150 verbatim.

E08.note: Record a retirement condition per vcpkg overlay port, naming the upstream event that lets it be deleted. Folds into #196, which is already going to touch the overlay to register it declaratively.

E09.note: Allocator as a vcpkg manifest FEATURE driven by the CMake option. B17 confirmed this is the right shape rather than deletion: mimalloc is LIVE here (source/CMakeLists.txt + StarMemory.cpp under STAR_USE_MIMALLOC), and removing it from the manifest reproduces in our tree the exact configure break their own PR scored against itself.

E10.note: Generated-and-gated provenance table for source/extern (version, upstream URL, why vendored, whether compiled). B12 supplied the concrete argument for the generated form over a hand-maintained one: THEIR extern/README.md contradicts their own vcpkg.json on its first policy bullet, asserting a builtin-baseline pin that their manifest does not carry -- false on the day it landed. Accepting this is also what fires D59/D60's trigger.
